question: Should ClawHub define and own an advisory declared-capability contract now, or wait for a shared OpenClaw or AgentSkills schema before exposing it through ingestion, APIs, and security review?
rationale: Field vocabulary, declaration authority, verification semantics, and the transition from advisory metadata to possible enforcement define a public security boundary that automation should not select on maintainers' behalf.

options.title: Align then adopt advisory schema
options.body: Agree on a shared versioned vocabulary, distinguish declared from observed or verified state, and roll it out as optional review metadata before considering enforcement.

options.title: Adopt a ClawHub-local schema
options.body: Ship a registry-specific optional schema now, accepting the future compatibility and migration cost if upstream contracts diverge.

options.title: Retain scanner-only review
options.body: Decline public capability declarations and continue relying on observed behavior, documentation review, and security findings.

recommendation.title: Align then adopt advisory schema
recommendation.body: Agree on a shared versioned vocabulary, distinguish declared from observed or verified state, and roll it out as optional review metadata before considering enforcement.

likelyOwner.reason: They previously authored the most directly related capability-manifest implementation and have repository-member association in the supplied history.
